en.display_text:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the nature of the Chittagong Conspiracy Case through which colonial authorities prosecuted members of Surya Sen's revolutionary group?

(a) It was tried before a Special Tribunal constituted specifically for the case — the same extraordinary mechanism used in the Lahore Conspiracy Case against Bhagat Singh's group
(b) It was tried through Bengal's criminal courts, with charges including waging war against the Crown, and resulted in the conviction of several members of Surya Sen's organisation including Surya Sen himself
(c) It was a civil suit filed by the colonial government to recover property and assets belonging to members of Surya Sen's organisation
(d) The trial was conducted in London under the jurisdiction of the Privy Council, which had special authority over sedition cases in the Indian provinces
en.strong_distractor: a — Option a is deceptive because the Lahore Conspiracy Case is the more famous 'conspiracy case' and students familiar with it may assume the Chittagong case operated through the same extraordinary special tribunal mechanism.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a): The Special Tribunal used to try Bhagat Singh in the Lahore Conspiracy Case was an extraordinary colonial legal instrument; the Chittagong Conspiracy Case was tried through Bengal's ordinary criminal courts, not the same special tribunal.
Eliminate option (c): The Chittagong Conspiracy Case was not a civil suit; it was a criminal prosecution for offences including waging war against the King.
Eliminate option (d): The Chittagong Conspiracy Case was tried in Bengal courts, not in London — the Privy Council was an appellate body, not the trial forum.

Retain option (b): The Chittagong Conspiracy Case was tried in Bengal's criminal courts, prosecuting members of Surya Sen's group for the armoury raid and associated acts including waging war against the Crown.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The conflation trap works by importing features of the more famous Lahore Conspiracy Case — specifically its extraordinary Special Tribunal — into the Chittagong Conspiracy Case. Students who know the Lahore case used a special tribunal (because the regular courts acquitted Bhagat Singh's associates in earlier proceedings) may assume the Chittagong case operated the same way. The key distinction is that the two cases went through different legal processes in different provincial jurisdictions.
en.final_explanation:
The Chittagong Conspiracy Case and the Lahore Conspiracy Case are frequently conflated by students, but they were distinct proceedings with different legal histories.

• Option (a) — Incorrect: The extraordinary Special Tribunal was a feature of the Lahore Conspiracy Case, where the colonial government bypassed regular courts after earlier acquittals by amending the Criminal Procedure Code. The Chittagong Conspiracy Case did not use the same special tribunal mechanism.
• Option (b) — Correct: The Chittagong Conspiracy Case was conducted through Bengal's criminal courts. Members of Surya Sen's group were tried for charges including waging war against the King, conspiracy, and related offences arising from the 1930 armoury raid and subsequent activities. Surya Sen was sentenced to death and executed in January 1934 following this case.
• Option (c) — Incorrect: This was a criminal prosecution, not a civil suit. Colonial authorities used criminal law, not civil litigation, to deal with armed revolutionaries.
• Option (d) — Incorrect: The trial took place in India, not in London. The Privy Council in London was a body to which convicted persons could appeal, not the trial forum.

Value Addition:
• The Lahore Conspiracy Case used a special tribunal constituted under the Criminal Law Amendment Act (1908) after regular courts failed to convict the accused.
• Kalpana Datta was tried in the Chittagong Conspiracy Case and sentenced to life transportation before being released in 1939.
• 'Waging war against the King' was the most serious charge available under colonial criminal law and carried the death penalty.

hi.upsc_trap_explanation: मिश्रण जाल (conflation trap) इस प्रकार काम करता है कि अधिक प्रसिद्ध लाहौर साजिश मामले की विशेष विशेष न्यायाधिकरण की विशेषता को चिट्टागाँव साजिश मामले में भी लागू मान लिया जाता है। जो छात्र जानते हैं कि लाहौर मामले में विशेष न्यायाधिकरण का उपयोग हुआ था (क्योंकि पहले के मुकदमों में भगत सिंह के साथियों को सामान्य अदालतों ने बरी कर दिया था), वे मान सकते हैं कि चिट्टागाँव मामले में भी ऐसा ही हुआ। मुख्य अंतर यह है कि दोनों मामलों की कानूनी प्रक्रिया और प्रांतीय अधिकार क्षेत्र अलग-अलग थे।
hi.final_explanation:
चिट्टागाँव साजिश मामला और लाहौर साजिश मामला अक्सर छात्रों द्वारा एकसाथ समझे जाते हैं, लेकिन ये अलग-अलग कानूनी प्रक्रियाएँ थीं जिनका इतिहास भिन्न था।

• विकल्प (a) — गलत: असाधारण विशेष न्यायाधिकरण लाहौर साजिश मामले की विशेषता थी, जहाँ औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने आपराधिक प्रक्रिया संहिता में संशोधन कर सामान्य अदालतों को दरकिनार किया था। चिट्टागाँव मामले में ऐसा विशेष न्यायाधिकरण नहीं था।
• विकल्प (b) — सही: चिट्टागाँव साजिश मामले की सुनवाई बंगाल के आपराधिक न्यायालयों में हुई। सूर्य सेन के समूह के सदस्यों को राजा के विरुद्ध युद्ध छेड़ने, साजिश रचने और 1930 के हथियार भंडार छापे से संबंधित अपराधों के लिए अभियोजित किया गया। सूर्य सेन को इस मामले के बाद जनवरी 1934 में फांसी दी गई।
• विकल्प (c) — गलत: यह एक आपराधिक अभियोजन था, कोई दीवानी मुकदमा नहीं। औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन ने हथियारबंद क्रांतिकारियों के खिलाफ आपराधिक कानून का उपयोग किया था, न कि दीवानी मुकदमे का।
• विकल्प (d) — गलत: मुकदमा भारत में हुआ था, लंदन में नहीं। लंदन का प्रिवी काउंसिल एक अपीलीय निकाय था, मुकदमे का मंच नहीं।

Value Addition:
• लाहौर साजिश मामले में आपराधिक कानून संशोधन अधिनियम (1908) के तहत विशेष न्यायाधिकरण गठित किया गया था क्योंकि सामान्य अदालतों ने अभियुक्तों को बरी कर दिया था।
• कल्पना दत्ता को चिट्टागाँव साजिश मामले में आजीवन कारावास की सजा हुई थी, जिन्हें 1939 में रिहा किया गया।
• 'राजा के विरुद्ध युद्ध छेड़ना' औपनिवेशिक आपराधिक कानून के तहत सबसे गंभीर आरोप था, जिसके लिए मृत्युदंड था।

shared.concept_anchor: Pritilata's farewell letter — themes and historiographical significance

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the significance of Pritilata Waddedar's written farewell statement:

1. Pritilata Waddedar's written statement before the Pahartali Club attack is significant as a historical source because it provides direct evidence of the ideological motivations of a woman revolutionary in her own voice — a rarity in the documentary record of the period.
2. The themes of Pritilata's farewell statement — motherland, sacrifice, and the equal duty of women in revolutionary action — reveal a purely emotional patriotism rather than a structured political thought, distinguishing her from more 'intellectually serious' male revolutionaries of the era.
3. The farewell letter's articulation of gender equality in revolutionary duty challenges the binary assumption that armed revolutionary action was inherently a masculine domain — making it relevant to feminist historiographical recovery projects.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Pritilata Waddedar's written statement before the Pahartali Club attack is significant as a historical source because it provides direct evidence of the ideological motivations of a woman revolutionary in her own voice — a rarity in the documentary record of the period.
statement_analysis.reason: The written statement is genuinely significant as primary evidence; most historical accounts of women revolutionaries are reconstructed through third-party memoirs, court records, or oral histories. A self-authored ideological statement from a woman combatant revolutionary is rare and historically valuable.

statement_analysis.statement: The themes of Pritilata's farewell statement — motherland, sacrifice, and the equal duty of women in revolutionary action — reveal a purely emotional patriotism rather than a structured political thought, distinguishing her from more 'intellectually serious' male revolutionaries of the era.
statement_analysis.reason: Feminist historians have specifically argued the opposite: Pritilata's statement reveals ideological clarity and structured political conviction, not mere emotional patriotism. The claim that her themes reflect 'purely emotional' rather than 'intellectually serious' reasoning reproduces the very domesticating interpretive framework that feminist historiography critiques.

statement_analysis.statement: The farewell letter's articulation of gender equality in revolutionary duty challenges the binary assumption that armed revolutionary action was inherently a masculine domain — making it relevant to feminist historiographical recovery projects.
statement_analysis.reason: Pritilata's explicit statement that women had an equal duty in revolutionary action directly challenges gendered assumptions about armed nationalism, and this is precisely why feminist historians have used it as evidence of women's political agency.

en.strong_distractor: b — Option b (1 only) tempts students who recognise Statement 1 as correct but are uncertain about Statement 3's historiographical claims, leading them to under-select.
elimination_logic: Statement 1 is correct — the written statement's rarity and its status as primary evidence in Pritilata's own voice is its key historical significance.

Statement 2 is incorrect — it reproduces a domesticating misreading that feminist historiography specifically critiques. Pritilata's statement demonstrates structured ideological thought, not mere emotional patriotism.

Statement 3 is correct — the letter's explicit claim to women's equal revolutionary duty challenges the male-armed-nationalist paradigm and is central to feminist historiographical use of the document.
Statements 1 and 3 are correct, making option (c) the answer.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 uses the partial-truth technique by embedding a recognisable fact (the themes of Pritilata's letter) within a false interpretive claim (that these themes reflect 'purely emotional patriotism'). A student who has read about Pritilata's letter may agree that it discusses motherland and sacrifice — true — without noticing that the characterisation of these themes as 'purely emotional rather than intellectually serious' is precisely the misreading that feminist historians have argued against. The partial truth is that the themes are correctly described; the false element is the reductive interpretation imposed on them.
en.final_explanation:
Pritilata Waddedar's farewell letter is a primary historical document of unusual significance, and its correct interpretation is itself a subject of historiographical debate.

• Statement 1 — Correct: The self-authored written statement is historically rare. Most women revolutionaries of the period left no direct textual record in their own voice — their motivations are reconstructed from court testimony, comrades' memoirs, or police records. Pritilata's statement is a primary document of a different order.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: The characterisation of Pritilata's ideological statement as 'purely emotional patriotism' rather than 'structured political thought' reproduces the very interpretive error that feminist historians have specifically diagnosed and critiqued. Scholars like Tanika Sarkar have argued that this kind of gendered reading — attributing rationality and intellectual seriousness to male revolutionaries while reducing women's motivations to emotion and self-sacrifice — must be challenged through careful reading of the evidence.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The letter's explicit articulation that women had an equal revolutionary duty challenges the assumption — prevalent in both colonial and nationalist discourse — that armed action was inherently male. This is why the document is central to feminist historiographical recovery projects.

Value Addition:
• Geraldine Forbes' 'Women in Modern India' (1996) is a foundational text for understanding how women's participation in nationalism — both violent and non-violent — has been framed and misframed.
• The distinction between 'primary sources' (documents from the period by the historical actors themselves) and 'secondary sources' (later reconstructions) is methodologically important for GS1 history questions.
• Pritilata's letter, alongside Bhagat Singh's prison writings and Aurobindo's political essays, represents the rare genre of the revolutionary's self-theorisation — documents where the actor explains their own actions in ideological terms.

hi.final_explanation:
प्रीतिलता वड्डेदार का विदाई पत्र एक असाधारण महत्व का प्राथमिक ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज़ है, और इसका सही व्याख्यान स्वयं इतिहासलेखकीय बहस का विषय है।

• कथन 1 — सही: स्वयं लिखित यह बयान ऐतिहासिक रूप से दुर्लभ है। उस काल की अधिकांश महिला क्रांतिकारियों ने अपनी आवाज़ में कोई प्रत्यक्ष लिखित अभिलेख नहीं छोड़ा — उनकी प्रेरणाएँ न्यायालय के साक्ष्य, साथियों की संस्मृतियों या पुलिस अभिलेखों से पुनर्निर्मित होती हैं। प्रीतिलता का बयान एक अलग श्रेणी का प्राथमिक दस्तावेज़ है।
• कथन 2 — गलत: प्रीतिलता के वैचारिक बयान को 'केवल भावनात्मक देशभक्ति' बताना और 'संगठित राजनीतिक विचार' न मानना वही व्याख्यात्मक त्रुटि है जिसकी नारीवादी इतिहासकारों ने विशेष रूप से पहचान की और आलोचना की है। तनिका सरकार जैसे विद्वानों ने तर्क दिया है कि पुरुष क्रांतिकारियों को तर्कशील और बौद्धिक गंभीर मानना जबकि महिलाओं की प्रेरणाओं को भावनात्मक और आत्म-बलिदान तक सीमित करना चुनौतीपूर्ण है और इसे सावधानीपूर्वक साक्ष्यों के अध्ययन से चुनौती दी जानी चाहिए।
• कथन 3 — सही: पत्र में स्पष्ट रूप से कहा गया है कि महिलाओं का क्रांतिकारी कर्तव्य समान है, जो उपनिवेशवादी और राष्ट्रवादी विमर्श दोनों में प्रचलित यह मान्यता चुनौती देता है कि सशस्त्र क्रांति स्वाभाविक रूप से पुरुषों का क्षेत्र है। इसलिए यह दस्तावेज़ नारीवादी इतिहासलेखन पुनर्प्राप्ति परियोजनाओं के लिए केंद्रीय है।

• 'प्राथमिक स्रोत' (काल के ऐतिहासिक पात्रों द्वारा लिखित दस्तावेज़) और 'माध्यमिक स्रोत' (बाद में पुनर्निर्माण) के बीच का भेद GS1 इतिहास प्रश्नों के लिए विधिवत महत्वपूर्ण है।

This question tests knowledge of women's leadership in armed or direct resistance movements across different national and historical contexts.

Correct matching:
• A (Constance Markievicz) → 3 (Irish revolutionary, military commander in the Easter Rising, 1916, against British colonial rule): Markievicz commanded the St. Stephen's Green garrison in the Easter Rising. She was sentenced to death but reprieved due to her gender — a fact that itself became politically charged.
• B (Sophie Scholl) → 1 (German civilian resistance figure, White Rose movement, arrested and executed in 1943 for distributing anti-Nazi pamphlets): Sophie Scholl was not an armed revolutionary but a civilian resistance figure who distributed anti-Nazi leaflets at the University of Munich. She was executed on February 22, 1943.
• C (Pritilata Waddedar) → 4 (Led armed squad at Pahartali European Club, 1932, disguised as a male Pathan soldier, died by self-administered potassium cyanide): The specific operational details confirm this pairing unambiguously.
• D (Kalpana Datta) → 2 (Surya Sen's Chittagong group, survived, tried in Chittagong Conspiracy Case, became a communist activist): Kalpana Datta's post-revolutionary trajectory — survival, trial, communist politics — is the defining feature of her pairing.

The trap pairing: A and B (Markievicz and Scholl) have swapped descriptions in options (a) and (b) — students who know both are European resistance women but are imprecise about which was Irish nationalist versus German anti-Nazi will be caught.

Value Addition:
• Markievicz was the first woman elected to the British House of Commons (December 1918) though she did not take her seat.
• The White Rose was a non-violent resistance movement; Sophie Scholl's action was civilian leafleting, not armed violence — an important distinction from Pritilata's armed squad.
• All four women defied the prevailing gender expectations of their respective societies and political movements.

सही मिलान:
• A (Constance Markievicz) → 3 (आयरिश क्रांतिकारी, 1916 के ईस्टर राइजिंग में सैन्य कमांडर, ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के खिलाफ): Markievicz ने ईस्टर राइजिंग में सेंट स्टीफन ग्रीन गढ़ को कमांड किया। उन्हें मृत्युदंड दिया गया था लेकिन लिंग के कारण माफी मिली — जो राजनीतिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण था।
• B (Sophie Scholl) → 1 (जर्मन नागरिक प्रतिरोध सेनानी, व्हाइट रोज़ आंदोलन, 1943 में नाजी-विरोधी पर्चे बांटने के लिए गिरफ्तार और फांसी दी गई): Sophie Scholl सशस्त्र क्रांतिकारी नहीं थीं बल्कि नागरिक प्रतिरोध सेनानी थीं जिन्होंने म्यूनिख विश्वविद्यालय में नाजी-विरोधी पर्चे वितरित किए। उन्हें 22 फरवरी 1943 को फांसी दी गई।
• C (Pritilata Waddedar) → 4 (1932 में पहरटली यूरोपियन क्लब में पुरुष पठान सैनिक के रूप में छद्मवेश में सशस्त्र दस्ते का नेतृत्व किया, घायल होने के बाद आत्महत्या के लिए पोटैशियम साइनाइड लिया): विशिष्ट परिचालन विवरण इस मिलान को स्पष्ट रूप से पुष्टि करते हैं।
• D (Kalpana Datta) → 2 (सूर्य सेन के चिट्टागाँव समूह की सदस्य, जीवित बचीं, चिट्टागाँव साजिश मामले में मुकदमा हुआ, कम्युनिस्ट कार्यकर्ता बनीं): Kalpana Datta का क्रांति के बाद का जीवन — जीवित बचना, मुकदमा, कम्युनिस्ट राजनीति — उनके मिलान की विशेषता है।

जाल मिलान: A और B (Markievicz और Scholl) के विवरण विकल्प (a) और (b) में उलट दिए गए हैं — जो छात्र जानते हैं कि दोनों यूरोपीय महिला प्रतिरोध सेनानियाँ हैं लेकिन यह स्पष्ट नहीं कर पाते कि कौन आयरिश राष्ट्रवादी और कौन जर्मन नाजी-विरोधी है, वे फंस जाएंगे।

• Markievicz ब्रिटिश हाउस ऑफ कॉमन्स में पहली महिला निर्वाचित थीं (दिसंबर 1918) हालांकि उन्होंने अपना स्थान नहीं लिया।
• व्हाइट रोज़ एक अहिंसक प्रतिरोध आंदोलन था; Sophie Scholl की कार्रवाई नागरिक पर्चा वितरण थी, सशस्त्र हिंसा नहीं — जो Pritilata के सशस्त्र दस्ते से महत्वपूर्ण भिन्नता है।
• ये चारों महिलाएं अपने-अपने समाजों और राजनीतिक आंदोलनों की लैंगिक अपेक्षाओं को चुनौती देती थीं।

en.display_text:
With reference to the final phase of the Chittagong revolutionary movement, consider the following statements:

1. Surya Sen was still an underground fugitive evading British capture at the time Pritilata Waddedar carried out and died in the Pahartali European Club attack of September 1932.
2. Pritilata Waddedar died in September 1932, and within weeks of her death, Surya Sen was captured, tried, and executed — the entire sequence completing before the end of 1932.
3. The elimination of leadership figures like Pritilata (who died in 1932) and Surya Sen (executed in 1934) significantly weakened the operational capacity of the armed revolutionary movement in Bengal.

Which of the above statements is/are NOT correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 3 only
(c) 2 only
(d) 1 and 3 only

statement_analysis.statement: Surya Sen was still an underground fugitive evading British capture at the time Pritilata Waddedar carried out and died in the Pahartali European Club attack of September 1932.
statement_analysis.reason: Surya Sen was captured only in February 1933 — approximately five months after Pritilata's death in September 1932. He was underground throughout the period of the Pahartali attack.

statement_analysis.statement: Pritilata Waddedar died in September 1932, and within weeks of her death, Surya Sen was captured, tried, and executed — the entire sequence completing before the end of 1932.
statement_analysis.reason: This statement compresses three distinct events falsely: Surya Sen was captured in February 1933 (not weeks after Pritilata's death), tried in the Chittagong Conspiracy Case, and executed in January 1934 — over a year after Pritilata's death, not within weeks of it and not before the end of 1932.

statement_analysis.statement: The elimination of leadership figures like Pritilata (who died in 1932) and Surya Sen (executed in 1934) significantly weakened the operational capacity of the armed revolutionary movement in Bengal.
statement_analysis.reason: The sequential loss of operational leaders — Pritilata through death in action, Surya Sen through capture and execution — is historically documented as a major factor in the decline of the Chittagong group's armed operations.

en.strong_distractor: a — Option a (only Statement 1 is incorrect) tempts students who correctly reject Statement 2 but are uncertain whether Statement 1 is precise about Surya Sen's status in September 1932, potentially doubting whether he was truly still underground at that point.
elimination_logic: Statement 1 is correct — Surya Sen was captured in February 1933, after Pritilata's September 1932 death; he was indeed still underground when she carried out the attack.

Statement 2 is incorrect — it falsely compresses Surya Sen's capture (February 1933), trial, and execution (January 1934) into 'within weeks' of Pritilata's September 1932 death. This is a significant temporal-swap error.
Statement 3 is correct — the sequential elimination of Pritilata and Surya Sen as leaders did weaken the Chittagong group's capacity.
Only Statement 2 is NOT correct, making option (c) the answer.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 uses the temporal-swap technique to compress a sequence of events spread across two years (September 1932 to January 1934) into a falsely condensed timeline ('within weeks,' 'before the end of 1932'). Students who know Pritilata died in 1932 and Surya Sen was executed 'sometime in the 1930s' without precise year knowledge will accept the false compression. The specific chronological precision required — September 1932 (Pritilata's death), February 1933 (Sen's capture), January 1934 (Sen's execution) — is exactly the level of detail UPSC chronology traps target.
en.final_explanation:
The precise timeline of the Chittagong movement's final phase is a frequent target for UPSC chronology traps, and this question tests whether students can detect false compression of that timeline.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Surya Sen evaded British capture for approximately two and a half years after the April 1930 armoury raid. He was underground in February 1933 — he was definitely still underground in September 1932 when Pritilata carried out the Pahartali attack.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: This statement falsely claims that Surya Sen was captured, tried, and executed 'within weeks' of Pritilata's death and 'before the end of 1932.' In reality: Pritilata died September 23, 1932; Surya Sen was captured February 1933; he was executed January 12, 1934. The entire sequence from Pritilata's death to Sen's execution spans over fifteen months — not weeks.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The loss of Pritilata (1932) and Surya Sen (1934) within two years constituted a severe blow to the operational capacity of the Chittagong revolutionary movement. Without its key figures, the organisation could not sustain its armed activities.

Value Addition:
• Surya Sen's evasion of capture for nearly three years after the armoury raid reflects the effectiveness of the movement's underground safe-house network in the Chittagong region.
• The period between Surya Sen's capture (February 1933) and execution (January 1934) was consumed by the Chittagong Conspiracy Case trial.
• Kalpana Datta's 1939 release came five years after Surya Sen's execution — reflecting how long colonial prosecutions could hold surviving members of revolutionary organisations.

2. प्रीतिलता वड्डेदार सितम्बर 1932 में मरीं, और उनकी मृत्यु के कुछ ही हफ्तों के भीतर सूर्य सेन को गिरफ्तार किया गया, मुकदमा चलाया गया, और फांसी दी गई — यह पूरी प्रक्रिया 1932 के अंत से पहले पूरी हो गई।
3. प्रीतिलता (जो 1932 में मरीं) और सूर्य सेन (जो 1934 में फांसी दिए गए) जैसे नेतृत्वकर्ताओं की समाप्ति ने बंगाल में सशस्त्र क्रांतिकारी आंदोलन की संचालन क्षमता को काफी कमजोर कर दिया।

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही नहीं है/हैं?

(a) केवल 1
(b) केवल 3
(c) केवल 2
(d) 1 और 3

statement_analysis.statement: Surya Sen was still an underground fugitive evading British capture at the time Pritilata Waddedar carried out and died in the Pahartali European Club attack of September 1932.
statement_analysis.reason: Surya Sen was captured only in February 1933 — approximately five months after Pritilata's death in September 1932. He was underground throughout the period of the Pahartali attack.

statement_analysis.statement: Pritilata Waddedar died in September 1932, and within weeks of her death, Surya Sen was captured, tried, and executed — the entire sequence completing before the end of 1932.
statement_analysis.reason: This statement compresses three distinct events falsely: Surya Sen was captured in February 1933 (not weeks after Pritilata's death), tried in the Chittagong Conspiracy Case, and executed in January 1934 — over a year after Pritilata's death, not within weeks of it and not before the end of 1932.

statement_analysis.statement: The elimination of leadership figures like Pritilata (who died in 1932) and Surya Sen (executed in 1934) significantly weakened the operational capacity of the armed revolutionary movement in Bengal.
statement_analysis.reason: The sequential loss of operational leaders — Pritilata through death in action, Surya Sen through capture and execution — is historically documented as a major factor in the decline of the Chittagong group's armed operations.

hi.strong_distractor: a — Option a (only Statement 1 is incorrect) tempts students who correctly reject Statement 2 but are uncertain whether Statement 1 is precise about Surya Sen's status in September 1932, potentially doubting whether he was truly still underground at that point.
elimination_logic: Statement 1 is correct — Surya Sen was captured in February 1933, after Pritilata's September 1932 death; he was indeed still underground when she carried out the attack.

Statement 2 is incorrect — it falsely compresses Surya Sen's capture (February 1933), trial, and execution (January 1934) into 'within weeks' of Pritilata's September 1932 death. This is a significant temporal-swap error.
Statement 3 is correct — the sequential elimination of Pritilata and Surya Sen as leaders did weaken the Chittagong group's capacity.
Only Statement 2 is NOT correct, making option (c) the answer.
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 uses the temporal-swap technique to compress a sequence of events spread across two years (September 1932 to January 1934) into a falsely condensed timeline ('within weeks,' 'before the end of 1932'). Students who know Pritilata died in 1932 and Surya Sen was executed 'sometime in the 1930s' without precise year knowledge will accept the false compression. The specific chronological precision required — September 1932 (Pritilata's death), February 1933 (Sen's capture), January 1934 (Sen's execution) — is exactly the level of detail UPSC chronology traps target.
hi.final_explanation:
The precise timeline of the Chittagong movement's final phase is a frequent target for UPSC chronology traps, and this question tests whether students can detect false compression of that timeline.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Surya Sen evaded British capture for approximately two and a half years after the April 1930 armoury raid. He was underground in February 1933 — he was definitely still underground in September 1932 when Pritilata carried out the Pahartali attack.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: This statement falsely claims that Surya Sen was captured, tried, and executed 'within weeks' of Pritilata's death and 'before the end of 1932.' In reality: Pritilata died September 23, 1932; Surya Sen was captured February 1933; he was executed January 12, 1934. The entire sequence from Pritilata's death to Sen's execution spans over fifteen months — not weeks.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The loss of Pritilata (1932) and Surya Sen (1934) within two years constituted a severe blow to the operational capacity of the Chittagong revolutionary movement. Without its key figures, the organisation could not sustain its armed activities.

Value Addition:
• Surya Sen's evasion of capture for nearly three years after the armoury raid reflects the effectiveness of the movement's underground safe-house network in the Chittagong region.
• The period between Surya Sen's capture (February 1933) and execution (January 1934) was consumed by the Chittagong Conspiracy Case trial.
• Kalpana Datta's 1939 release came five years after Surya Sen's execution — reflecting how long colonial prosecutions could hold surviving members of revolutionary organisations.
